entry: Diagnosis from the 0.3.1 tables. On the six xenografts the same-species ratio is 1.77 at the default budget and 1.34 with the budget at zero (0.3.0 with no budget: 0.90). So the false-positive budget is the largest single part: 0.4% of native counts is about 40% of the background of a library that has 1% background. On the xenograft library that was opened (xeno_HSC_3) about 44% of the expected background is the swapped-read term, which stayed at its starting value because five tested genes cannot separate it from the depth-proportional ambient term. The expected same-species background on xenografts is the cross-species counts times about ten (the ambient RNA is 9% human), so the ratio itself is less certain there than on cell-line mixtures.

Two changes written. (1) A gene's false-positive allowance is at most 20% of its own expected background (fpr_background_cap); a gene with no expected background gives up nothing. At 2 to 3% background, as in the tuning mixtures, this leaves the allowance about where it was. (2) The swapped fraction starts at 0.0002 in the silent-gene fit instead of the learned value (swap_start), so it grows only where silent-gene counts ask for it.

Unit tests pass on an HPC3 compute node (new test: capped allowance). First round submitted on 23 development libraries: the default twice, without the cap, and with the old start of the swapped fraction.

First round scored (15 development mixtures; 0.3.1, then the two replicates of the new default). Same-species ratio 1.02 to 0.90 and 0.92; cross-species removal 89.1% to 86.6% and 89.0%; per-cell error 0.0188 to 0.0183 and 0.0160. By library the cap does little for the clean tissue it was meant for (xeno_HSC_1 ratio 0.93 to 0.87; xeno_HSC_3 1.62 to 1.61 and 1.24, a spread between two runs of the same code) and it leaves BD Rhapsody under-cleaned (ratio 1.01 to 0.72): there the model expects too little same-species background and the allowance was making up for it. The small start of the swapped fraction changes little on its own. Unstable libraries remain: parse_hgmm_sub1 got an estimate in one replicate and none in the other (removal 90% and 56%).

Where the extra removal on xeno_HSC_3 comes from: the truth says about 1.6% of counts are background; the model expects 1.3 to 1.5%, but 2.4% is removed. The difference is the allowance (0.4%) and the wider silent set: a gene was called silent when its cluster count fits the ridge level times the fitted background, and the ridge level on this library is 1.77. With doublet-like cells already out of the cluster sums that factor has no place, so a gene with up to 1.8 times the fitted background was stripped in full. Second round: the wider set is tested against the fitted background itself (silent_wide_level = 1), with and without the cap, two replicates each.

Second round scored (15 development mixtures). Testing the wider silent set against the fitted background does not fix the xenograft (same-species ratio on xeno_HSC_3 1.33 and 1.40 with the cap, 1.61 and 1.47 without; 0.3.1 1.62) and costs removal elsewhere: parse_hgmm_sub1 89.5% to 70% and 63%, kidney tubule-marker removal 87% to 83-84%. The cap on the allowance leaves BD Rhapsody under-cleaned again (ratio 0.66) and, because the output keeps each cell's background total, pushes removal onto marker genes (nuclei mixture: marker counts kept in their own cells 99% to 76%). Both are set aside: the defaults go back to no cap and the ridge level. The small start of the swapped fraction stays (with the old start parse_igvf_NOOZ lost 16.5% of its counts in one run, 2% otherwise).

The actual cause, found by listing the cells that lose far more than their true background. On xeno_HSC_3, 7 to 32 of the 1,816 scored cells (about 1%) lose 92 to 99% of their counts, which is 11 to 28% of all counts removed from the library. They are the human immune cells of the xenograft (MALAT1, B2M, FTH1, HLA-DRA, CD74, S100A8/9, LYZ). The library is clean, so the silent-gene fit uses only three clusters; the few human cells sit in mouse clusters, every human gene is silent there, and the exclusion constraint strips them. All of these cells already carry the doublet-like flag (far more counts on silent genes than background explains), but since 0.3.1 flagged cells were still held to the silent genes, because sparing all of them left the most contaminated cells of BD Rhapsody and Parse uncleaned. How many are hit depends on the clustering, which explains the spread between repeat runs.

Fix written (0.3.2.dev3). For each flagged cell the gene profile of its silent-gene counts is compared with the fitted background profile on those genes (overlap of the two distributions, divided by the overlap expected when the counts are Poisson draws from the background profile; about 1 for background, low for a second expression program). Cells below the threshold (doublet_match, 0.5) are left alone: no exclusion constraint, trend multiplier, flagged in the output; cells above it are heavily contaminated and stay held to the silent genes. In a two-cell-line mixture the other species' ambient profile and cell profile are alike, so those cells stay cleaned; in tissue a rare cell type or a doublet partner expresses only part of what the soup holds. Unit test: background-like cells score 0.99, second-program cells at most 0.17. Third round submitted on the 23 development libraries: threshold 0.5 twice, 0.7 twice, and every flagged cell spared once.

Third round scored (15 development mixtures and 5 kidney libraries). The profile test does what it was written for: per-cell error on xeno_HSC_3 0.060 (0.3.1) to 0.024 and 0.024 at threshold 0.5, 0.021 and 0.020 at 0.7, 0.017 with every flagged cell spared (CellBender 0.020); counts removed 2.4% to 2.0% (truth 1.6%); the two replicates now agree. Heavily contaminated cells stay cleaned at 0.5: BD mix 1 removal 91.0% and 91.9% (88.3% with every flagged cell spared), parse_hgmm_sub1 90.4% and 84.6% (65.7%); at 0.7 the Parse mixture loses 5 to 10 points. Kidney unchanged (removed over truth 0.99 and 1.00; tubule markers 88%). Mean per-cell error over the 15 mixtures 0.0188 to 0.0164. Threshold 0.5 is kept.

What the profile test misses on xeno_HSC_3: about 14 flagged cells per run score 0.5 to 0.9 and still lose a third of their counts (truth 1.5%; 8% of all removal). They are human cells in mouse clusters whose silent genes are mostly human genes, and the background on human genes came from cells like them, so their counts resemble it. Flagged cells of the BD and Parse mixtures with the same scores carry 10 to 30% background by the species truth, so the score alone cannot separate the two. What does: a contaminated cell still looks like its cluster on the genes the cluster expresses, a misplaced cell does not. Second test added (cluster match): the share of a flagged cell's counts that its cluster's own expression explains; below 0.3 the cell is left alone.

Two calibration failures seen across the 13 development runs so far. (1) parse_igvf_NOOZ lost 11% and 17% of its counts in two runs, 2% in the other eleven. In those two runs two of the three clusterings gave a background level 1.7 to 3 times the usual one, and their final ridge (the level read against the fit) was 8.9 and 11 where every sound clustering on every library ends between 1.1 and 3.6. A clustering whose final ridge is above 5 now does not count (fewer clusters are tried next). (2) The Parse mixtures had no estimate in 4 of 16 runs because only one cluster showed silent genes; a single cluster is now accepted as a last resort. Not solved and recorded as a limit: parse_bm_hfd, a dirty eight-sublibrary Parse library with no truth, where the estimate of a sublibrary falls to a fifth of its usual value in about a quarter of the runs (a small group of genes forms a lower peak).

Unit tests pass (cluster match over own share: members at least 0.97, strangers at most 0.14). Fourth round submitted on the 23 development libraries: the new default four times, to measure the spread between runs, and the cluster match threshold at 0.5 twice. CellBender 0.4.0 has finished on all 54 libraries, each with its filtered output at three budgets.

Fourth round scored (six runs: the default four times, cluster match 0.5 twice). Calibration: parse_hgmm_sub2 has an estimate in all six runs (three of them from a single cluster; 4 of the 10 earlier runs had none) and removal 67 to 73% (54% without an estimate); parse_igvf_NOOZ lost 1.5 to 2.1% of its counts in all six (11% and 17% in 2 of the 13 earlier runs), with the convergence check setting a clustering aside in two of them. Still without an estimate in one run of six: xeno_HSC_1 (removal 71% there, 89 to 91% otherwise). The cluster match test changed little: xeno_HSC_3 per-cell error 0.023 to 0.025 at 0.3 (0.024 without it) and 0.020 to 0.021 at 0.5, where parse_hgmm_sub1 lost removal (69% and 80% against 85 to 88%); 4 to 7 xenograft cells still lose a third of their counts. They are mouse cells of rare kinds whose own genes are silent in their cluster; the rest of their expression looks like the cluster, so the test passes them. The cluster match is switched off.

What separates the flagged cells that are rightly stripped from those that are not is the amount. Flagged cells that stay held to the silent genes, by the share of their counts removed, against the truth of the scored ones (round four, replicate a): below 15% removed, the truth says at least as much background (BD mix 1: 7.1% removed, truth 10.7%; Parse mixtures 8 to 11% against 21 to 34%; six 10x mixtures 8 to 13% against 12 to 22%; kidney_rep1 12.5% against 17.8%, kidney_rep2 13.6% against 12.0%); 15 to 20%, kidney only, about even (17.3% against 16.9%, 17.4% against 13.9%); above 20%, far more is removed than is background wherever it can be measured (xeno_HSC_3 26.8% and 35.6% against 0.6% and 1.3%; kidney_rep1 23% and 43% against 8% and 15%; kidney_rep2 24% and 33% against 13% and 15%; kidney_nuc3 28% and 33% against 5%). In the cell-line mixtures no scored cell is above 15%: such a cell fails the 90% purity rule and counts as a multiplet. Rule added: a flagged cell with more than 20% of its counts on silent genes is left alone (doublet_share_max). Fifth round submitted, three replicates. HPC3 is reached through the office Studio since about 02:00 (the VPN dropped; Tailscale is up).

Fifth round scored (three replicates of the final rule). xeno_HSC_3: cells stripped far beyond their true background 32 in 0.3.1, 4 to 7 in round four, 1 in each replicate now; per-cell error 0.0166, 0.0173, 0.0174 (0.3.1 0.0595; CellBender 0.0195); counts removed 1.86%, 1.74%, 1.78% (truth 1.58%; 0.3.1 2.38%); same-species ratio 1.24, 1.16, 1.19 (0.3.1 1.62). Mean per-cell error over the 15 development mixtures 0.0158 to 0.0160 (0.3.1 0.0188; CellBender 0.0401), lower than CellBender on 14 of 15. BD mix 1 removal 90.1%, 91.4%, 91.2% (0.3.1 88.6%). Kidney unchanged: removed over truth 1.00, 1.00, 1.00 (kidney_rep2 still 1.24 to 1.29), tubule markers 87 to 88%. The cost: parse_hgmm_sub1, where the number of flagged cells depends on the clustering (215 to 406 of 4,190), removal 70.7%, 88.6%, 77.5% against 85 to 90% without the cap. In the two low runs about 240 to 300 flagged cells have more than 20% of their counts on silent genes and are left alone; the scored ones among them carry 8.5 to 12.5% background by the species truth, so trend-level cleaning (3 to 5%) leaves them under-cleaned by about as much as stripping (more than 20%) over-cleaned them. Per-cell error there 0.027 and 0.026 against 0.023.

Glymph 0.3.2 frozen. Against 0.3.1: (1) a cell with far more counts on its cluster's silent genes than background explains is left alone, and flagged, when those counts do not follow the background profile (match below 0.5) or are more than a fifth of the cell; otherwise it is cleaned as before; (2) the swapped fraction starts at 0.0002 in the silent-gene fit; (3) a clustering whose level and fit disagree more than fivefold at the end does not count; (4) a single cluster with silent genes is accepted when no clustering offers two. Tested and not adopted, kept as options that are off: the cap on the false-positive allowance, the wider silent set tested against the fitted background, the cluster match. Known limits carried into the benchmark: libraries with few tested genes still vary between runs (xeno_HSC_1 had no estimate in 3 of 11 runs and then removes 71% instead of 89 to 91%; parse_hgmm_sub1 as above; parse_bm_hfd, where a sublibrary's estimate drops to a fifth in about a quarter of runs); kidney_rep2 is over-cleaned 1.2 to 1.3 times; one xenograft cell in 1,816 still loses more than three times its background plus 3 points. Run on all 54 libraries beside CellBender 0.4.0: 20261117-1342_glymph-cb040-bench.
